Article Title: $3.64 billion pulled from world's largest crypto exchange Binance after $6.3 billion heist
Article Text:
The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange is seeing signs of easing withdrawal pressure after customers rushed to move 2.1 per cent of its total assets off the platform

Customers withdrew $3.64 billion from Binance after hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from wallets held at the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange last week, triggering an initial rush of withdrawals as users moved to protect their assets. Binance said the outflows were now stabilising as it resumed services following the security breach.The withdrawals accounted for around 2.1 per cent of Binance's total assets. The exchange, which had $171 billion in assets under management as of October 28, said deposit volumes had remained "substantial" despite the initial spike in withdrawals."(That) puts the withdrawals in the range of a precautionary reaction rather than any sort of capital flight," Ari Redbord, global head of policy at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, said, as quoted by Reuters.The pace of withdrawals is being closely watched as an early indicator of whether customers continue to trust the platform following one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record.Binance has sought to reassure users that the financial damage from the breach would not be passed on to them. The company said it had replaced around 95 per cent of the stolen assets using its own funds, spending approximately $6 billion to buy replacement tokens.The remaining 5 per cent comprises less liquid cryptocurrencies that could take longer to source in the required quantities.The exchange resumed withdrawals in phases on Sunday, initially allowing transactions involving 15 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, Dogecoin and some stablecoins such as USDT and USDC. Binance said it was prioritising tokens based on user demand over the past week."We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand," the exchange said in a post on X, adding, "Rest assured that market conditions are stable."However, data from crypto analytics platform DefiLlama showed higher outflows of $5.81 billion, up from the $4.36 billion it had reported earlier. Binance disputed the figures, saying they did not account for certain deposits into its new hot wallet."This figure does not contain the flows we have deposited to our own new hot wallet, so they are not accurate. Our last update on X is closest to accurate," a Binance spokesperson said.The broader cryptocurrency market also showed signs of recovering after the initial shock. Bitcoin, which touched a six-week low on Friday, traded above $78,000 on Monday, while Ether recovered to around $2,287 after hitting a two-month low.Meanwhile, the combined market capitalisation of the two largest stablecoins, USDT and USDC, declined by around $1.2 billion since Friday, according to CoinMarketCap.Binance has said it will bear the financial cost of the breach, setting aside approximately $6.34 billion from its corporate treasury, Futures Insurance Fund and Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to cover the losses.
Article Summary: Customers withdrew $3.64 billion from Binance after hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency. The withdrawals accounted for around 2.1 per cent of Binance's total assets. Binance said the outflows were now stabilising as it resumed services following the security breach.

Article Title: Reliance shares surge over 7%, eye best single-day gain since January 2024: What's driving the rally?
Article Text:
Reliance shares climbed to Rs 1,237.45 on the BSE, up 6.35 per cent at 10:22 am on Monday.

According to Google Trends, searches for ‘reliance share price’ surged by over 5,000% in India.

Shares of Reliance Industries surged over 7 per cent in early trade on Monday after the company reported a record quarterly profit for July-September. The stock jumped 7.12 per cent to Rs 1,246.45 on the BSE and 6.79 per cent to Rs 1,244 on the NSE. The rally added Rs 1,00,208.45 crore to the company's market capitalisation, taking it to Rs 16.74 lakh crore.The gains followed Reliance's record September-quarter performance, with consolidated profit, including the share of associates and joint ventures, rising 33.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 29,550 crore. Net profit attributable to owners of the company increased 40 per cent to Rs 25,548 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 27.8 per cent to Rs 3.62 lakh crore, while EBITDA climbed 23.9 per cent to a record Rs 62,409 crore.The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business was the biggest driver of the performance. Its segment EBITDA jumped 67.9 per cent to Rs 25,203 crore, while revenue increased 44.2 per cent to Rs 2.32 lakh crore. Stronger transportation fuel refining margins and improved petrochemical margins amid global supply disruptions supported the recovery.The rally in Reliance also lifted the broader market. At 10.24 am, the BSE Sensex was up 935.82 points at 75,390.02, while the NSE Nifty had gained 248.15 points to 23,300.05.Jefferies said O2C “hit the bullseye”, citing record crude processing, flexible sourcing and a shift towards higher-value fuel exports that helped Reliance benefit from favourable refining conditions. The brokerage raised its earnings forecasts following the stronger-than-expected results.Emkay Global also pointed to the sharp recovery in O2C and improving profitability at Jio as key drivers of the earnings beat. It raised its estimates and maintained that the stock's valuation remained attractive.Retail continued to be the softer part of the business. Reliance Retail's gross revenue rose 6.4 per cent to Rs 91,716 crore, but EBITDA before a one-time impairment charge declined 8.6 per cent to Rs 6,228 crore. Investments in digital commerce, higher input costs and the shift of major festivals to the December quarter weighed on performance. JioMart, however, recorded 42 per cent revenue growth.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)
Article Summary: Reliance shares climbed to Rs 1,237.45 on the BSE, up 6.35 per cent at 10:22 am on Monday. Google Trends, searches for ‘reliance share price’ surged by over 5,000% in India.

Article Title: India among world's best-performing markets in October as investors rotate away from AI stocks: Goldman Sachs
Article Text:
AI-linked stocks trail as IT services power India's October rally

Indian equities were reportedly among the world's best-performing markets in October, outperforming the broader Asia-Pacific region as investors shifted money away from AI-sensitive technology stocks and towards other sectors. The trend was also visible within India, where IT services stocks gained ground while companies linked to the AI ecosystem lagged, according to a Goldman Sachs Research report.The Nifty outperformed the broader Asia-Pacific region excluding Japan (MXAPJ) by 7 percentage points, reversing its underperformance during the first nine months of 2026.The change in investor preference was particularly sharp within India's technology space. Stocks classified as AI enablers, which had beaten the Nifty by 76 percentage points between January and September, underperformed the benchmark by 6 percentage points in October. IT services companies moved in the opposite direction, outperforming the index by 14 percentage points to become the month's leading sector.Goldman Sachs attributed India's gains to a broader shift in global portfolios. “India benefited from market rotation away from AI-sensitive North Asian markets,” the report said, describing the country as one of the world's best-performing markets in October, as cited by ANI.The recovery followed a difficult third quarter, when the Nifty had fallen 10 per cent from its peak to its trough. It recovered 3 per cent from its early-October low. Momentum continued in the week ended October 30, with the benchmark gaining 2 per cent against a 1 per cent rise in MXAPJ.The latest advance was not limited to large-cap stocks. Mid-cap and small-cap shares rose 3-4 per cent during the week, while pharmaceuticals gained 7 per cent. Financial stocks were relatively subdued, advancing just 1 per cent.Institutional flows also showed signs of improvement. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought $1.2 billion worth of Indian equities during the week, although their net outflows for 2026 remained high at $31 billion. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) added $400 million, taking their purchases for the year to $75 billion.Earnings have provided another source of support. Companies accounting for 58 per cent of the MSCI India index's market capitalisation had reported their July-September results by the time of the report. Their combined profits were tracking 15 per cent higher than a year earlier and 13 per cent above the previous quarter.The performance, however, was uneven. Metals and mining, utilities and healthcare companies delivered more positive surprises, while cement and materials and consumer discretionary firms reported more earnings misses.The rally has also made Indian equities expensive relative to regional peers. The market's forward price-to-earnings ratio stood at 18.4 times, while its valuation premium over the broader Asia-Pacific region reached 92 per cent, close to historical highs.With several large companies due to announce results in early November, investors will be looking for earnings to justify the market's elevated valuations.
Article Summary: Indian equities were reportedly among the world's best-performing markets in October. Investors shifted money away from AI-sensitive technology stocks and towards other sectors. The trend was also visible within India, where IT services stocks gained ground while companies linked to the AI ecosystem lagged, according to a Goldman Sachs Research report.

Article Title: 'We will navigate through challenges': IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh on airline industry's tough phase
Article Text:
IndiGo sees growth potential despite industry headwinds, focuses on cost control

IndiGo focuses on costs amid elevated fuel expenses

A350 deliveries and Navi Mumbai airport plans

IndiGo sees significant growth opportunities despite rising fuel costs and other pressures facing the aviation industry, CEO Willie Walsh said on Monday, adding that the airline would focus on maintaining a competitive cost base while navigating the challenges.At his first in-person briefing since taking charge as chief executive in August, Walsh said IndiGo expected to begin receiving wide-body Airbus A350 aircraft from the second quarter of 2028.He said the airline had all the necessary ingredients to succeed in the long-haul market."We see incredible opportunities," Walsh said, while acknowledging the difficult operating environment for airlines.The industry is facing pressure from higher fuel costs, which have affected airline profitability. IndiGo reported a net loss of Rs 1,879.1 crore in the July-September quarter, with elevated fuel expenses and rupee depreciation weighing on its financial performance."The situation is challenging for the industry and we will continue to navigate through the challenges," Walsh said.The airline has also reduced capacity in response to the operating pressures. In the September quarter, its fuel expenses rose to Rs 9,966.8 crore, an increase of 67.2% from Rs 5,961.8 crore in the corresponding period last year.IndiGo's capacity, measured in available seat kilometres, declined 1% to 40.8 billion during the quarter.Despite a 4.7% fall in passenger numbers to 2.7 crore, passenger ticket revenue increased 29.3% to Rs 20,652.2 crore, while the load factor declined 2.2 percentage points to 80.3%.Walsh had said last week that the airline expected elevated fuel costs to persist for some time and would continue exploring internal measures to offset the increase.The airline's September-quarter loss was its third consecutive quarterly loss, as per the earlier report. Its total income, however, rose 24% year-on-year to Rs 24,311.9 crore.On IndiGo's expansion plans, Walsh said the airline expected deliveries of its wide-body A350 aircraft to begin in the second quarter of 2028. He said the carrier was well placed to enter the long-haul market.Walsh also described the upcoming Navi Mumbai airport as a significant opportunity for the airline. He said IndiGo's decision to shift some of its international flights to the new airport had been taken in the airline's interest.IndiGo currently operates more than 2,100 flights daily and has an operational fleet of over 400 aircraft.As of September 30, the airline had a fleet of 442 aircraft and operated a peak of 2,020 daily flights during the July-September quarter, including non-scheduled services.The airline's cash balance stood at Rs 52,685.4 crore at the end of September, comprising Rs 39,929 crore in free cash and Rs 12,756.4 crore in restricted cash. Its total debt, including capitalised operating lease liabilities, was Rs 87,303.1 crore, the report said.
Article Summary: IndiGo sees significant growth opportunities despite rising fuel costs and other pressures facing the aviation industry. CEO Willie Walsh said the airline would focus on maintaining a competitive cost base while navigating the challenges. IndiGo expected to begin receiving wide-body Airbus A350 aircraft from the second quarter of 2028.

Article Title: Transferred Post Office employees posed as authorised staff, collected money for fake NSCs and term deposits in Rs 36.4 lakh fraud; Madhya Pradesh HC directs Post Office to process victims' claims
Article Text:
The fraud came to light later, when the depositors discovered that the documents they had received were forged and that no accounts had actually been opened. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the depositors succeed in their case?

Imagine a scenario where you open some post office savings accounts, but it turns out that the accounts are fake because the people who took the deposits were not authorised to do so and scammed you!In a recent ruling by the Madhya Pradesh High Court some people at the India Post Office's Bina branch duped several depositors by issuing them counterfeit National Savings Certificates (NSCs) and term deposit advice slips. The fraud involved approximately Rs 36.4 lakh.According to the submissions made before the court, the depositors had visited the Bina post office intending to invest in a term deposit account and a National Savings Certificate (NSC). Before they could approach the counter, however, some employees approached them, offered to assist with the paperwork and collected the money from them. These employees allegedly misrepresented their authority and subsequently handed over fabricated account statements and passbooks to the customers.The fraud came to light later, when the depositors discovered that the documents they had received were forged and that no accounts had actually been opened in their names. Despite the losses suffered by the customers, the Department of Posts declined to return their money, according to an ET report.The department argued that the depositors had dealt with an employee who had already been transferred and was no longer posted at the Bina branch when the transactions took place.According to the postal authorities, customers should have approached the authorised officials at the counter instead of relying on employees who were not assigned to that branch.The affected depositors, however, maintained that the fraud had been carried out through the actions of postal department employees. They argued that the department should therefore bear vicarious liability and compensate them for the financial losses caused by the fraudulent activities of its staff.The advocate representing the depositors argued that there was no dispute over the fact that the forged passbooks had been issued and the purported accounts opened through individuals who were employees of the Department of Posts.The depositors had no reason to doubt the identity or authority of these individuals, he contended. They could not reasonably have been expected to know whether an employee present at the post office was officially posted at that particular branch.The lawyer representing the postal department opposed the claims for compensation. The department maintained that it could not be held responsible for the money lost because the victims had not carried out their NSC and term deposit transactions through authorised staff at the counter. Instead, they had dealt with employees who were not posted at the Bina branch at the time.Madhya Pradesh Police arrested the employees responsible, who were subsequently prosecuted and convicted. Despite this, the postal department declined to compensate the affected depositors, arguing that they had failed to check whether the employees were authorised to operate at the Bina post office.The department acknowledged that the individuals involved were its employees but maintained that they had not been officially assigned to the Bina branch. However, these employees were present on the premises and allegedly targeted customers visiting the post office to open NSC and term deposit accounts.The victims eventually secured relief from the Madhya Pradesh High Court on October 15, 2026. The court directed the Department of Posts to return the money lost by the depositors, along with applicable interest.Nivedita Bhardwaj, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the depositors won because the Madhya Pradesh High Court accepted that they had acted in good faith and conducted their transactions with individuals who were employees of the postal department. The employees had assisted them in opening accounts and issued passbooks, which were subsequently discovered to be fake. The employees were later prosecuted and convicted for their role in the fraud.The High Court pointed out that an ordinary depositor could not be expected to have knowledge of the department's internal transfer and posting arrangements, particularly when the employees concerned were present inside the post office, according to the ET report on the judgement.The Madhya Pradesh High Court said an examination of the case records showed that the depositors had been approached at the post office by individuals who were admittedly employees of the Department of Posts. The customers had no knowledge of whether these employees were assigned to the Bina branch, nor could they be expected to know about the department's internal posting arrangements.The Madhya Pradesh High Court said: “Therefore, once the petitioners (victims) acted bona fide and innocently and opened their accounts with the concerned Post Office at the behest of the said persons who were later found to be culprits, the petitioners (victims) were entitled for the amount as claimed by them after the fraud was committed.”It also referred to the department's circular dated May 27, 2021, which specifically lays down a procedure for handling situations in which an account has not actually been opened or a fraudulent passbook has been issued.On this basis, the High Court directed the postal department to entertain the claims submitted by the victims. It instructed the depositors to complete the prescribed form and submit it to the competent authority within 30 working days. Once the applications are received, the authority must examine and process the claims within 90 days.The court further held that the victims would be entitled to interest applicable to their fixed deposits, in accordance with the law.Bhardwaj said depositors should take care to route all their investments through the authorised channels of the post office. They should also collect and retain official records relating to their deposits, including passbooks, deposit receipts, account particulars and other transaction acknowledgements.Bhardwaj says: "In cases involving a fake passbook or an account that was never actually opened, depositors should also make use of the claim mechanism prescribed by the Department of Posts. The present judgment makes it clear that such situations are specifically contemplated under the Department's May 27, 2021 circular."
Article Summary: The fraud involved approximately Rs 36.4 lakh. Despite the losses suffered by the customers, the Department of Posts declined to return their money. The department argued that the depositors had dealt with an employee who had already been transferred and was no longer posted at the Bina branch.

Article Title: Gold price prediction today: Will gold continue to fall? Check outlook for November 2, 2026 week
Article Text:
Attention now shifts towards the US midterm elections and upcoming labour-market data.

Gold price prediction

today:

Gold prices

are likely to continue trading sideways with a downward bias, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. Let’s take a look at his detailed analysis:

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Gold enters week near Rs 138,500 after extending its October correction, with the hourly structure continuing to reflect a clear sequence of lower highs and lower lows. Prices have declined sharply from above Rs 151,000 earlier in October and are currently trading well below the 20-period average near Rs 140,660, confirming continued selling pressure.The Bollinger Bands are placed around Rs 143,877 on the upside and Rs 137,442 on the downside, with prices trading close to the lower band after the latest breakdown. Immediate support is placed around Rs 137,400–138,000, followed by Rs 135,000–136,000; a sustained break below this zone could expose Rs 132,000–133,000.On the upside, Rs 140,500–141,000 is now the first important hurdle, followed by Rs 143,000–144,000. A sustained recovery above Rs 144,000 would be required to meaningfully improve the short-term structure and could open the way towards Rs 146,000–147,000.Overall, the near-term technical bias remains sideways to lower below Rs 141,000, although the magnitude and speed of the recent correction increase the possibility of short-covering or a technical rebound. For the broader structure, reclaiming Rs 144,000–146,000 would be necessary before considering the correction to be stabilising.Gold enters the week attempting to recover towards $3,900 following another sharp correction, with bargain hunting and persistent geopolitical uncertainty providing support at lower levels. However, the broader macro environment remains challenging as a liquidity adjustment across global markets has triggered selling across multiple asset classes.The recent AI-led correction in technology shares has encouraged investors to reduce risk and meet margin requirements, resulting in profit-booking across gold and silver following their substantial earlier rallies. This helps explain why bullion has struggled to benefit fully from equity-market weakness and geopolitical uncertainty, as gold has temporarily been used as a source of liquidity rather than purely as a safe-haven asset.Treasury yields remain another major headwind. Long-dated US yields near 5.5% offer investors increasingly attractive risk-free returns while simultaneously tightening financial conditions beyond the Federal Reserve’s policy rate. Elevated yields increase gold’s opportunity cost and have contributed to the recent liquidation.At the same time, persistently high borrowing costs are increasing concerns over US debt-servicing expenses, fiscal sustainability and eventually economic growth. This creates a mixed environment: yields remain negative for gold in the immediate term, but the fiscal consequences of sustaining such high rates could strengthen bullion’s longer-term diversification case.Monetary policy remains restrictive after the Fed kept rates unchanged at 3.75%–4.00%, while retaining the possibility of another increase if inflation remains persistent.The absence of a clear dovish pivot keeps real yields elevated and leaves bullion sensitive to incoming inflation and labour-market data. Markets will therefore closely monitor whether softer economic activity begins to outweigh persistent inflation risks in determining the next policy move.Geopolitical risks continue to provide an underlying floor. Uncertainty surrounding US–Iran relations and the broader Middle East remains supportive of defensive demand, although gold’s response has been restrained by the stronger influence of yields and liquidity conditions.Meanwhile, dip buying from Chinese investors and longer-term strategic buyers appears to be emerging following the substantial correction, helping prices stabilise around lower levels.Attention now shifts towards the US midterm elections and upcoming labour-market data. The election outcome could materially influence expectations surrounding fiscal policy, government spending, Treasury issuance and political uncertainty, while employment data will be important in determining whether the Fed retains room for another hike.Overall, gold remains vulnerable to elevated real yields and further cross-asset liquidation in the near term, but bargain hunting, geopolitical uncertainty, Chinese demand and growing concerns surrounding US fiscal sustainability could provide an increasingly important floor following the sharp October correction.
Article Summary: Gold prices are likely to continue trading sideways with a downward bias, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. Prices have declined sharply from above Rs 151,000 earlier in October. Attention now shifts towards the US midterm elections and upcoming labour-market data.

Article Title: LTCG tax relief on the cards? SEBI wants long-term capital gains tax to be removed for foreign investors
Article Text:
Indian equities have underperformed other emerging markets over the past two years.

Stock market turmoil

The buzz around removal of long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on equities is gaining traction, with the market regulator also urging the government to scrap it. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has reportedly requested the government to consider scrapping LTCG tax levied on foreign investors.The proposal comes as authorities look for ways to revive India's equity markets, which have been performing below the level of their emerging market counterparts.According to a Reuters report, SEBI has also suggested extending tax relief to domestic mutual fund investors. Under its proposal, investors switching from existing mutual fund holdings to other schemes would not have to pay LTCG tax on the transaction, sources quoted in the report said.The recommendations have been submitted ahead of the annual Union Budget scheduled for February. However, they are advisory in nature, and the final decision on whether to accept them rests with the government.Indian equities have underperformed other emerging markets over the past two years. Foreign investors have withdrawn a record $31 billion from Indian stocks so far this year, while retail investors have increased their overseas investments as domestic market returns have remained subdued.SEBI's proposals follow numerous discussions the regulator has held with foreign investors over the past two years, even as continued selling by overseas funds has put pressure on the Indian currency.A recurring concern raised during these interactions has been India's tax treatment of foreign investors, the sources said."The proposals are aimed at reducing the upfront tax burden on foreign investors," one of the two sources told Reuters.SEBI has pointed out that the costs of investing in Indian equities are among the highest when compared with other markets.At present, investors are required to pay LTCG tax of 12.5% on securities held for more than a year. Short-term capital gains are taxed at 20%. These levies are in addition to securities transaction taxes on trades and withholding taxes on dividend income.In a note issued earlier this week, brokerage firm Jefferies said lowering capital gains taxes could make Indian equities more appealing to overseas investors and help attract portfolio inflows.Brokerage IIFL has estimated that doing away with capital gains tax could increase foreign investors' returns by 2.3 percentage points.The underperformance of Indian equities has also affected domestic investors. The benchmark Nifty 50 has fallen 4.8% over the past two years, whereas the MSCI emerging markets index has gained 40%.Returns from diversified domestic equity mutual funds, which have become a popular investment avenue among retail savers, have remained weak during the same period. Data from fund research firm Morningstar shows that large-cap mutual funds have delivered average returns of minus 1.6%.SEBI wants to encourage investors to continue investing in domestic mutual funds. To achieve this, it has been proposed that moving investments from one mutual fund scheme to another should not trigger a tax liability, provided the original units have been held for more than a year, the sources said.The domestic mutual fund industry currently manages assets worth Rs 82.6 trillion ($870.80 billion). Monthly investment schemes bring in an average of Rs 30 billion every month.
Article Summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has reportedly requested the government to consider scrapping LTCG tax levied on foreign investors. The proposal comes as authorities look for ways to revive India's equity markets. Indian equities have underperformed other emerging markets over the past two years.

Article Title: India's manufacturing PMI eases to 54.7 in October as export orders hit six-month high
Article Text:
Strong overseas demand cushions slowdown in India’s manufacturing activity (representative image)

Output rises, but hiring growth remains subdued

Input cost inflation falls to lowest since February

Business confidence weakens

India's manufacturing activity expanded at a slower pace in October as growth in output and new orders moderated, although stronger overseas demand supported production and helped cushion the slowdown.Factory employment continued to rise, while input cost inflation eased to its lowest level since February, a monthly survey showed on Monday.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global, fell to 54.7 in October from 55.1 in September.Despite the decline, the index remained above its long-run average and comfortably higher than the neutral mark of 50, which separates expansion from contraction.Growth in new business remained strong, although it eased marginally from September's seven-month high. New export orders, however, increased at their fastest pace in six months, according to the survey.Manufacturers reported higher demand from markets including Bangladesh, Canada, Indonesia, Nepal, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, the UK, the US and the UAE."Strong international demand pushed growth of new export orders to a six-month high, supporting a robust rise in output," said Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC.Stronger overseas demand supported an increase in factory output, although the pace of production growth softened from September. The survey attributed the rise in new business to favourable demand trends, new client wins and successful marketing campaigns.Manufacturers continued to build inventories during the month. Input inventories increased at the fastest pace in eight months as companies built precautionary buffers against potential shortages and prepared to meet production requirements in a volatile global environment.Firms also increased their stocks of finished goods at a record pace in the survey's more than 21-year history, according to Reuters. Manufacturers cited buoyant demand and efforts to prevent shortages.However, the pace of raw material purchasing growth slowed to its weakest in the 64-month sequence of expansion.Factory employment increased for the second consecutive month as higher production requirements and rising workloads encouraged companies to recruit more workers. However, the pace of job creation eased from September.Capital goods manufacturers reduced staff during the month.Cost pressures moderated across all three broad areas of India's manufacturing industry monitored by the survey. Although manufacturers reported higher prices for some materials and energy, the overall rate of input cost inflation declined to its lowest level since February.Selling price inflation also weakened. The increase in output prices was the slowest in nearly four years."Although some material and energy costs increased, overall input and output price pressures eased slightly from the previous month," Bhandari said.Despite continued growth in demand, manufacturers became less optimistic about the year ahead. Business confidence slipped from September and remained below its long-run average, the survey said.Close to 18 per cent of manufacturers expected output to increase over the coming year, while the rest were neutral. Expectations of higher production were supported by new client enquiries and demand for industrial automation and technology solutions.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global from responses to questionnaires sent to purchasing managers at a panel of around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 54.7 in October from 55.1 in September. Factory employment continued to rise, while input cost inflation eased to its lowest level since February. Business confidence slipped from September and remained below its long-run average.

Article Title: China to restrict exports of giant tunnel-digging machines; why India could be affected
Article Text:
Representative image

Why the restrictions matter for India

India looks to reduce dependence on Chinese machinery

Domestic manufacturing faces cost challenges

China is tightening export controls on construction equipment, including tunnel-boring machines, in a move that could affect India's infrastructure projects and add to concerns over its dependence on Chinese machinery.The new restrictions cover specialised equipment used to build tunnels for roads, railways and metro networks, as well as machines designed to spray concrete at high altitudes.Beijing has cited the potential military as well as civilian applications of such equipment, warning that "sensitive countries and regions with disputes with China" will face stricter export rules, Bloomberg reported.The curbs are particularly significant for India, which is among China's major customers for tunnel-boring equipment and is expanding road and railway infrastructure along the Himalayan border.The two countries have a longstanding territorial dispute in the region, where India has been building connectivity infrastructure to reduce the time required to mobilise troops.The latest restrictions are due to take effect later this month, according to Bloomberg. They also cover components, raising concerns not only about fresh procurement but also the maintenance of machinery already in use.Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution, said Beijing increasingly viewed its position as a major global construction equipment producer in strategic terms."It raises the risks of dependency, and incentivizes other countries to try to de-risk from China," Chan said.China accounts for around 70% of the global tunnel-boring machine market, according to Chinese state media figures cited by Bloomberg. Its leading manufacturer, China Railway Engineering Equipment Group Co Ltd, says its machinery is used in 36 countries, including Denmark and France.India has previously faced delays in procuring Chinese-made tunnelling equipment.In 2024, China delayed efforts by German manufacturer Herrenknecht AG to sell tunnel-boring machines to India for projects including the Ahmedabad-Mumbai bullet train and the Delhi Metro.A spokesperson for Herrenknecht said the company was studying the latest Chinese restrictions.The new controls could also affect the supply of spare parts. Ajay Srivastava, founder of the New Delhi-based Global Trade Research Initiative, said India could shift equipment between priority projects if necessary, but restrictions on components could create difficulties for existing machinery."When there is heavy wear and tear in these machines we require regular supply of parts," Srivastava said, adding that the curbs could affect both the existing stock of machines and the procurement of new ones.The inclusion of equipment used for concrete spraying at high altitudes has also drawn attention. Sun Chenghao, a fellow at Tsinghua University's Center for International Security and Strategy in Beijing, said this could indicate a particular focus on "strategically sensitive terrain"."For China, the central concern is where Chinese engineering capabilities are used and whether they could strengthen another country's military infrastructure," Sun said.The restrictions come as India seeks to expand domestic manufacturing of high-value construction and infrastructure equipment.The government is considering a $1.2-billion incentive scheme for manufacturers of equipment such as tunnel-boring machines, firefighting systems and elevators.The proposed programme is expected to attract around $1.8 billion in fresh investment by offering incentives to domestic manufacturers over seven years. It is also expected to include local value-addition targets for machinery that is currently imported.The scheme was announced in the 2026-27 Union Budget as part of efforts to strengthen domestic production of technologically advanced construction and infrastructure equipment. State-run BEML, along with private-sector companies such as Larsen & Toubro and Johnson Lifts, could benefit from the proposed incentives, according to the earlier report.India's infrastructure expansion is expected to drive demand for specialised equipment. Road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari has said the country aims to invest up to $9.6 billion in tunnelling over the next five years and has urged domestic industry to manufacture tunnel-boring machines.Larsen & Toubro, one of India's major engineering companies, is working on developing its own tunnel-boring machine.R Shankar Raman, president of the Mumbai-based company, said L&T was building a prototype and could eventually manufacture machinery for its own projects and other buyers if the experiment proved successful.However, he cautioned that India's manufacturing industry was still at an earlier stage, while Chinese manufacturers benefited from large-scale production."If people are still going to compare with Chinese price and find ways to import from China," Raman said, "then India will be at a disadvantage."Bloomberg Economics said the restrictions could slow some infrastructure projects, including strategic construction along the disputed Himalayan border.However, it also noted that tighter Chinese export controls could strengthen India's case as an alternative manufacturing base, encouraging foreign equipment makers to add capacity in the country.Besides Herrenknecht, manufacturers in the US and Japan also produce potential alternatives to Chinese tunnelling equipment. However, switching suppliers in the short term could be difficult for customers that rely heavily on Chinese machinery.
Article Summary: China is tightening export controls on construction equipment, including tunnel- boring machines. The move could affect India's infrastructure projects and add to concerns over its dependence on Chinese machinery. The restrictions are due to take effect later this month. They also cover components, raising concerns about fresh procurement and maintenance of machinery.

Article Title: At 1,000 this fiscal, IndiGo set to hire most pilots in a year by an Indian carrier
Article Text:
IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh, a trained pilot will spearhead the budget airline’s international expansion

NEW DELHI: In the largest ever cockpit crew hiring by an Indian airline, IndiGo has on boarded 600 pilots in the first six months of this fiscal and is on track to add at least 400 more by next March-end. The airline had committed to add pilots after witnessing an unprecedented schedule collapse last Dec. IndiGo had 5,700 pilots as on March 31, 2026, and this number rose to 6,300 by Sept end.The flight duty time limitation (FDTL, which regulate pilot duty norms) dispensation will end next March and IndiGo’s CEO Willie Walsh said on Monday in his first interaction with the media in this role that the airline will have “more than enough pilots to meet the schedules that we have for the airline. We're confident that of fully complying with the FDTL regulations.”A trained pilot, Willie — who headed British Airways and International Air Transport Association before joining IndiGo this Aug — will spearhead the budget airline’s international expansion over coming years amid the unprecedented challenges being faced by aviation globally. IndiGo, which used to be India’s only profitable airline, has also flown into losses for the past few quarters.“The geopolitical situation is challenging. Aviation turbine fuel accounts for 32% of airlines’ operating cost globally. In India, that figure is higher at 40%. The concerning thing is the crack spread (price difference between a barrel of crude oil and the petroleum products like ATF refined from it). Crude prices have not gone that high but the premium on ATF pricing has risen. Luckily availability of ATF is not an issue in India which exports jet fuel,” said Walsh.Airlines have not fully passed on the hike in operating cost and have taken other measures like cutting capacity in the lean travel July-Sept quarter. Also due to geopolitical reasons flights have been cut. Saudi flights are impacted right now, with IndiGo also cutting the same.“No Indian carrier does fuel hedging. We are weighing that option for long hauls expansion. We expect to get our Airbus A350s from the second quarter of 2028. As of now we have four A321 XLRs (extra long range) and will get more of these planes next year,” said Walsh. IndiGo has 60 A350s on firm order. “We will have a business class with 16 flat bed seats, premium economy and economy sections in the first 10 A350s. Then we will see whether to increase the number of business class seats in subsequent deliveries. I personally think there will be a case of doing so,” said Walsh.The closure of Pakistan airspace for Indian carriers has impacted western routes to and from Delhi. Air India and IndiGo now add flights to the west mainly from Mumbai. “The Navi Mumbai airport is a business opportunity for IndiGo as our long haul international expansion in the future will be also from Mumbai and Navi Mumbai (apart from other places like Delhi and Bengaluru).”Walsh, however, cautioned overall airport charges in India are “too high.” “Indian aviation market will do much better with lower charges and taxes,” he said.
Article Summary: IndiGo has on boarded 600 pilots in the first six months of this fiscal and is on track to add at least 400 more by next March-end. The airline had committed to add pilots after witnessing an unprecedented schedule collapse last Dec. IndiGo, which used to be India’s only profitable airline, has flown into losses for the past few quarters.

Article Title: India, EU begin talks on customs cooperation ahead of trade pact signing set for next month
Article Text:
The India–EU deal is India’s largest-ever trade pact, in terms of the number of countries covered.

India and the European Union have begun discussions on customs procedures and other arrangements needed to implement their free trade agreement (FTA), ahead of its planned signing in December.The discussions took place during Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal's visit to Brussels last week, where he met senior officials from three European Commission departments dealing with trade, international partnerships, and taxation and customs.The meetings focused on customs cooperation, trade facilitation and preparations for putting the India-EU trade pact into effect, the commerce ministry said on Monday.Emphasising the importance of smoother cross-border trade, the ministry said, “Both sides recognised the importance of efficient, transparent, and digitally enabled customs procedures in supporting businesses, reducing transaction costs, and ensuring the smooth movement of legitimate trade,” as quoted by PTI.The visit also included discussions with representatives of the diamond industry linked to Antwerp, one of the world's major diamond trading centres.The talks covered the global diamond supply chain, certification and traceability standards, responsible sourcing, and opportunities emerging from India's expanding diamond market and manufacturing base.India and Belgium have identified gems and jewellery as an important area for closer cooperation, with Antwerp, Mumbai and Surat recognised as key diamond centres.The India-EU FTA negotiations were formally concluded on January 27. Once implemented, the agreement is expected to provide duty-free access to Indian labour-intensive sectors, including textiles, leather and gems and jewellery.
Article Summary: India and the European Union have begun discussions on customs procedures and other arrangements needed to implement their free trade agreement. The discussions took place during Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal's visit to Brussels last week. Once implemented, the agreement is expected to provide duty- free access to Indian labour-intensive sectors, including textiles, leather and gems and jewellery.

Article Title: India's RE policies a role model for emerging economies: Analysis
Article Text:
India is actively seeking to attract $220 billion in investments to expand its renewable energy sector.

Emerging market financing for renewables

NEW DELHI: As India looks to attract international investment and deepen cooperation in clean energy, green hydrogen, storage and manufacturing at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE), a new international analysis has described the country as a “role model” in developing its renewable power sector, crediting its policy and regulatory measures for addressing investment risks and creating an environment conducive to private capital.The assessment comes at a time when India is looking to mobilise around $220 billion in investment between 2027 and 2030 to expand renewable energy capacity, manufacturing, transmission infrastructure and energy storage as it works towards its target of 500 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. Govt has already secured $64 billion in private investment between June 2024 and June 2026, including $6.2 billion in foreign direct investment, MNRE secretary Santosh Sarangi told reporters earlier this week.The recent analysis by Zero Carbon Analytics, titled, said India had adopted a holistic approach to addressing risks related to project development, construction and market access, describing the country as “a renewables powerhouse built on enabling policies”.The report said India's long-term target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, backed by an annual bidding trajectory of 50 GW of renewable energy capacity through FY28, provides visibility to developers and investors.It also highlighted govt’s decision to allow up to 100% foreign direct investment in the electricity sector.Among the measures aimed at reducing project development risks, the analysis cited the Ultra Mega Renewable Energy Power Parks scheme, which provides developers access to land and transmission infrastructure, along with capital and interest subsidies for renewable energy projects. It also pointed to viability gap funding for offshore wind projects, including support for the development of India's first offshore wind farms.On the demand side, the report said renewable consumption obligations, which require distribution companies and large industrial and commercial consumers to source a specified proportion of their electricity from renewable sources, have helped create an expanding market for green power. Access to day-ahead and intra-day power exchanges has also widened avenues for generators to sell electricity.The analysis also highlighted measures introduced by govt in 2022 to address delays in payments by distribution companies to power generators, which had been a major concern for renewable energy developers. Outstanding dues of distribution companies, which stood at Rs 1.4 lakh crore in 2022, declined to Rs 4,109 crore in Feb 2026, it said.The report estimated that capital expenditure on solar and onshore wind projects across emerging and developing economies could reach $356 billion by 2040 if current trends continue.A senior industry executive said India’s policies to boost investment in the renewable energy sector over the past two decades had catalysed green energy growth and helped the country meet its Paris Agreement goals ahead of schedule. “Further investment focus is now required in the country’s solar supply chain. India will continue to lead in renewable energy growth and investment attractiveness, thanks to the conducive policy environment and resilience of the Indian solar industry,” the executive said.
Article Summary: India is looking to mobilise around $220 billion in investment between 2027 and 2030 to expand renewable energy capacity, manufacturing, transmission infrastructure and energy storage. Govt has already secured $64 billion in private investment between June 2024 and June 2026, including $6.2 billion in foreign direct investment.

Article Title: Centre likely to meet FY27 fiscal deficit target despite despite higher spending: Goldman Sachs
Article Text:
Goldman expects strong tax collections and spending controls to keep the Centre on track to meet its FY27 fiscal deficit goal.

The Centre is likely to meet its fiscal deficit target of 4.3 per cent of GDP for FY27 despite recording 42.6 per cent of its full-year budgeted deficit in the first six months, with stronger corporate tax collections providing a cushion against revenue pressures, Goldman Sachs Research said in a report.The investment firm expects the government to manage its finances through expenditure reprioritisation, even as higher interest payments and capital spending weigh on the fiscal position. However, a sustained rise in global commodity prices could complicate the exercise by pushing up fertiliser subsidies and prompting further fuel excise duty relief."We continue to expect the central government to stick to the 4.3% of GDP fiscal deficit target, most likely through re-prioritisation of spending," the report said, as quoted by ANI.The Centre's fiscal deficit between April and September stood at 3.9 per cent of GDP, or 42.6 per cent of the full-year budget estimate. While the pace was higher than in recent years, it remained below pre-pandemic levels, Goldman Sachs noted.A significant improvement was visible in September, when the government's fiscal position was balanced, compared with a deficit of Rs 2.6 lakh crore in August. Stronger direct tax collections, particularly from corporates, helped offset higher interest payments and capital expenditure.Direct tax receipts rose 13 per cent year-on-year in September, supported by a 27 per cent jump in corporate tax collections. Income tax receipts, however, contracted 8 per cent during the month.The trend has been more pronounced in corporate tax collections during the financial year so far. These have grown around 22 per cent year-on-year, significantly above the 12 per cent growth estimated in the Budget. Income tax collections, meanwhile, increased around 9 per cent, falling short of the budgeted growth projection of 18 per cent.The stronger corporate tax performance has helped compensate for the revenue impact of lower excise collections following reductions in petrol and diesel duties.On the expenditure side, capital spending increased 17 per cent month-on-month on a seasonally adjusted basis in September, although it remained 3 per cent below the year-ago level, largely due to lower allocations towards roads and highways. For the April-September period, capital expenditure growth stood at 12.7 per cent.Overall government expenditure rose 12 per cent year-on-year in September, while subsidy spending declined 31 per cent, reflecting lower outgo on food and fertilisers.Goldman Sachs flagged energy prices as a potential source of pressure on government finances. A prolonged increase in global commodity prices could raise the fertiliser subsidy burden and increase the possibility of additional fuel tax relief, making expenditure management more challenging.The Centre's ability to contain spending pressures while sustaining tax revenue growth will therefore remain crucial to meeting its FY27 fiscal deficit target.
Article Summary: The Centre is likely to meet its fiscal deficit target of 4.3 per cent of GDP for FY27. Stronger corporate tax collections provide a cushion against revenue pressures. A sustained rise in global commodity prices could complicate the exercise by pushing up fertiliser subsidies and prompting further fuel excise duty relief.

Article Title: GST changes from November 1: Easier registration for online sellers, faster refunds and simpler discount rules
Article Text:
Easier registration for small e-commerce sellers, faster refunds

Easier GST registration for small online sellers

GST registration to become simpler

Faster GST refunds with automated approvals

NEW DELHI: Starting November 1, businesses will see several changes in Goods and Services Tax (GST) procedures, with simpler registration, faster refunds and more flexible rules for discounts offered after a sale.The changes, approved at the 57th GST Council meeting on October 8, are aimed at making GST compliance easier, particularly for small businesses and sellers operating through e-commerce platforms.The reforms mainly cover GST registration, returns and refunds, along with the tax treatment of post-supply discounts. The Council's decisions requiring administrative changes will be implemented in phases beginning Sunday, November 1, 2026.Small businesses selling products through e-commerce platforms across multiple states and Union Territories will no longer need to maintain a physical office in every state where their goods are stored.Under the new rules, eligible sellers passing on input tax credit of up to Rs 2.5 lakh per month can use an e-commerce operator's warehouse as their principal place of business (PPoB) for GST registration in states where they do not have a physical presence.However, sellers must have a genuine physical presence in at least one state, where Aadhaar authentication and physical verification will be carried out. For other states, they can obtain GST registration with the consent of the e-commerce platform, without further involvement of a tax officer.The change is expected to benefit around 9.5 lakh small sellers, helping them expand their reach across India without the additional cost of setting up offices in multiple states. It is also expected to create greater tax parity between competing e-commerce business models.Businesses applying for GST registration can also expect a smoother process from November 1.The GST department has standardised the documents and information required for registration, making it easier for applicants to understand what they need to submit.The GST portal will also offer a more user-friendly interface, with clearer navigation, drop-down lists and tooltips to guide applicants through the process.These changes are expected to reduce errors, unnecessary queries and application rejections caused by missing or incorrect information, while speeding up registration approvals.Businesses waiting for GST refunds could receive their money faster under the new system, which reduces the need for manual intervention by tax officers.Refund claims for the full excess balance available in a taxpayer's electronic cash ledger will be sanctioned automatically by the system, without requiring approval from a tax officer.Similarly, for refund claims related to zero-rated supplies and an inverted duty structure, 90% of the claimed amount will be provisionally sanctioned through an automated process.These provisional refunds will be based on the system's identification and assessment of risks, without direct intervention from tax officers.The government is also easing GST rules for post-supply discounts, addressing a longstanding concern among businesses.Under the revised framework, businesses will have greater flexibility to offer discounts after a sale without having to meet the earlier requirements of a pre-existing agreement or linking the discount to specific invoices.However, safeguards related to credit notes and the corresponding reversal of input tax credit will remain in place.The change is expected to benefit businesses that regularly offer volume-based incentives, trade schemes and year-end rebates.
Article Summary: GST reforms mainly cover GST registration, returns and refunds, along with the tax treatment of post-supply discounts. Small businesses selling products through e-commerce platforms across multiple states and Union Territories will no longer need to maintain a physical office in every state.

Article Title: China's 3 biggest airlines slip into losses as jet fuel prices more than double
Article Text:
China's leading airlines are experiencing significant financial losses amid rising jet fuel prices and weak domestic fare competition. (Pic Credit: ANI)

Rising fuel costs weigh on earnings

Intense competition keeps fares under pressure

China's three biggest airlines are heading towards another year of losses after reporting a sharp deterioration in their third-quarter financial performance, with soaring jet fuel prices, weak domestic airfares and typhoon-related disruptions weighing on earnings during the peak travel season.Air China and China eastern airlines are on course to record their seventh consecutive annual net loss since the Covid-19 pandemic, according to analyst estimates compiled by LSEG. China Southern Airlines, which returned to profitability in 2025 for the first time since 2019, is also expected to slip back into the red.Air China's third-quarter net profit dropped 92.6% year-on-year to 270.6 million yuan ($40.62 million). China Eastern reported a quarterly net profit of 64 million yuan, marking a 98.2% decline from the corresponding period last year.China southern, meanwhile, posted a net loss of 609 million yuan for the July-September quarter, compared with a profit of 3.84 billion yuan a year earlier.All three carriers recorded losses during the first nine months of 2026, reversing the profits they had reported over the same period in 2025.The July-September period, which coincides with China's busy summer travel season, is traditionally the most profitable quarter for the country's airlines. However, the carriers said a steep increase in jet fuel prices had adversely affected their financial results.Jet fuel prices have more than doubled since the US and Israel launched a military campaign against Iran in late February. Chinese airlines, which hedge a much smaller proportion of their fuel requirements than several Asian and European counterparts, are particularly exposed to fluctuations in oil prices.Domestic airfares also remained weak during the quarter amid stiff competition from other airlines and high-speed rail services.Huatai Securities estimated that air china's yields, an indicator of average fares, declined 5% during the period, making it difficult for the carrier to offset higher fuel expenses.Nathan Gee, head of asia-pacific transport research at BofA Global Research, said Chinese airlines were likely to remain loss-making in the seasonally weaker fourth quarter because of elevated jet fuel costs.He noted that third-quarter earnings had been marginally better than already subdued market expectations. Industry checks indicated that domestic fares had risen at double-digit rates year-on-year following the October Golden Week holiday, as airlines restrained capacity.However, Gee said fuel costs continued to be the biggest challenge, adding that airline margins remained under severe pressure from expensive jet fuel and subdued consumer demand.Airlines are seeking to increase the number of flying hours per aircraft to manage expenses, but opportunities for significant cost reductions remain limited, he said.Shares of Air China, China eastern and China southern have fallen 38%, 46% and 39%, respectively, so far this year.
Article Summary: Air China and China eastern on course to record their seventh consecutive annual net loss since the Covid-19 pandemic. China Southern Airlines, which returned to profitability in 2025 for the first time since 2019, is also expected to slip back into the red. All three carriers recorded losses during the first nine months of 2026.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Crude falls over 1% as Iran-Qatar talks raise hopes of diplomatic progress
Article Text:
Representative image

Iran-Qatar talks and Strait of Hormuz disruptions

Opec+ keeps December output targets unchanged

Oil prices fell more than 1% on Monday as Iranian and Qatari officials held talks for a third consecutive day aimed at securing an agreement to end the US-Israeli war on Iran, easing some immediate concerns over supply disruptions.Brent crude futures declined $1.59, or 1.40%, to $111.84 a barrel by 0011 GMT.US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell $1.56, or 1.50%, to $102.56 a barrel, according to Reuters.The decline followed a strong rise last week, with Brent ending October at its highest level in six months amid concerns that the conflict between the US, Israel and Iran could escalate again after Tuesday's US midterm elections.Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade, said the fall reflected a technical correction after last week's gains, alongside hopes of progress in diplomatic efforts."Oil is seeing a technical pullback this morning after last week’s strong gains," Waterer said, as quoted by Reuters."Lingering hopes of some form of diplomatic progress, combined with the absence of any meaningful military escalation over the weekend, have taken some of the immediate heat out of prices for now."However, he cautioned that the market remained alert to the possibility of stronger rhetoric over Iran, which could push Brent crude towards $120 a barrel after the midterm elections.The latest price movement came as Iranian and Qatari officials continued consultations aimed at facilitating an agreement to restart direct negotiations between Washington and Tehran.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" discussions was to continue consultations with Qatari mediators. He added that Tehran was prepared for "both defence and diplomacy".The diplomatic efforts are taking place against the backdrop of attacks on oil tankers travelling through the Strait of Hormuz, which have pushed up global energy and shipping costs.The waterway is a key route for global oil shipments, and disruptions to tanker movements have remained a concern for energy markets during the conflict.Meanwhile, the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and its allies, a grouping known as Opec+, kept their December production targets unchanged on Sunday.The decision was in line with market expectations and indicated that the group would not make further policy adjustments until next year, as it continues to face export disruptions linked to the Iran war.Separately, Saudi Arabia increased its crude oil exports in October compared with September, despite attacks by Iran-aligned Yemeni Houthi forces on its energy infrastructure, Reuters reported, citing two of three ship-tracking companies.The developments in the Gulf, the outcome of diplomatic efforts involving Iran and Qatar, and the possibility of renewed military escalation after the US midterm elections remain key factors for oil markets.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures declined $1.59, or 1.40%, to $111.84 a barrel by 0011 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell 1.50%, or $102.56 a barrel. The decline followed a strong rise last week, with Brent ending October at its highest level in six months.

Article Title: Binance resumes Bitcoin withdrawals after $6.3bn hack, says 95% of assets replaced
Article Text:
The first phase covers 15 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, XRP and Dogecoin.

FBI links $6.3 billion hack to North Korean hackers

Binance uses company funds to cover losses

Binance thanks US agencies for tracking stolen funds

Binance resumed withdrawals of Bitcoin, Ether and some stablecoins on Sunday after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from the exchange. The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange said it had replaced 95 per cent of the stolen assets using its own funds, while withdrawals of other cryptocurrencies would resume in phases.The first phase covers 15 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, XRP and Dogecoin. Bitcoin withdrawals resumed shortly after 0600 GMT, followed by Ether, BNB and some stablecoins, including USDT and USDC.Binance said it had spent around $6 billion buying replacement tokens. The remaining 5 per cent of stolen assets comprises less liquid cryptocurrencies that could take longer to source in the required quantities.The FBI on Saturday attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a cyber unit sponsored by the North Korean state. The agency said it had observed members of the group converting stolen assets into Ether and expected further attempts to launder the funds.North Korea has repeatedly denied using state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue generation. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis had also linked the attack to North Korea. They said most of the theft took place within around 20 minutes late on Thursday, bearing similarities to previous cyberattacks attributed to the country.However, US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Washington was not yet certain whether North Korea was involved.Binance said it had been working with industry partners to freeze the stolen assets, with around $3 billion located by Friday. The exchange has repeatedly assured customers that it would absorb the financial losses rather than pass them on to users.The company has set aside around $6.34 billion to cover the damage. Funds used to buy replacement tokens came from its corporate treasury, part of its Futures Insurance Fund and its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a reserve designed to protect customers during security breaches.Binance co-CEO Yi He said on Saturday that half of the SAFU funds would be used, with the company committing to replenish the reserve to around $1 billion.Binance thanked the FBI for its assistance in a post on X referring to the agency's statement on North Korea's alleged involvement. The exchange did not respond to a request for comment on the attribution.Founder Changpeng Zhao also credited US law enforcement agencies with helping track and freeze the stolen assets."A tweet can't fully express our gratitude. Many crypto bros may not realize, a lot of the 'why bitcoin didn't drop more?' credit goes to them," Zhao wrote.Zhao was convicted in the US of failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering programme at Binance. US President Donald Trump pardoned him last year.The attack comes amid a wider rise in cryptocurrency thefts. Researchers at TRM Labs estimated that hackers stole around $2.9 billion in digital assets across nearly 150 attacks last year.
Article Summary: Binance resumes withdrawals of Bitcoin, Ether and some stablecoins on Sunday. The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange said it had replaced 95 per cent of the stolen assets using its own funds. The FBI on Saturday attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a cyber unit sponsored by the North Korean state.

Article Title: Binance to resume withdrawals after recovering 95% of $6.3 billion crypto theft
Article Text:
Representative image

FBI links crypto heist to North Korean hacking unit

Trump says investigators are still examining North Korea link

Binance promises customers full reimbursement

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has said it will resume withdrawals in phases after securing 95% of the $6.3 billion in digital assets stolen from its platform in what is being described as the world's largest cryptocurrency heist.The first phase of withdrawals will begin between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday and cover bitcoin, ether, BNB, Solana, XRP, dogecoin and several other tokens, Reuters reported.The exchange said the remaining 5% of the stolen assets comprised less liquid tokens that could take longer to source in the required quantities.Binance announced the update in a post on X late on Saturday.The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has attributed the cyberattack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit.The bureau said on Saturday that members of the group had been observed converting the stolen assets into Ethereum.In a statement, the FBI identified TraderTraitor as responsible for the attack and said it expected further attempts to launder the stolen funds using related technology.The bureau also urged cryptocurrency exchanges, blockchain analytics companies and other industry participants to block transactions associated with identified addresses to prevent the stolen money from being moved to conceal its origins.The FBI said its investigation found that the hackers were converting the stolen assets primarily into Ethereum. It expects the group to attempt further conversions through decentralised finance (DeFi) platforms and instant swap services.TraderTraitor has also been linked to a $1.5 billion hack of cryptocurrency exchange Bybit last year.North Korea has for years denied using state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue generation.US President Donald Trump appeared to question whether North Korea's involvement in the Binance attack had been established.Asked about the incident by reporters at a Halloween party at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Saturday night, Trump said, “I'm not concerned. We're learning about it. We don't know if it's North Korea.”He added that investigators could still determine whether Pyongyang was responsible.Crypto expert Ari Redbord was quoted by news agency AP as saying that he expected the hackers to break the stolen assets into smaller amounts and attempt to move them through smaller exchanges to evade detection. The process could continue for months, he said.“It's bank robbery, in this case, at the speed of the Internet,” said Redbord, chief policy officer at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs.He added that investigators could track the funds in real time to build cases, disrupt laundering attempts and potentially recover the assets.“It's just this cat and mouse game,” he said.The theft took place on Thursday, when $6.3 billion in bitcoin and other digital currencies was stolen from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.The company said on Saturday that it had set aside enough of the same digital currencies to cover 90% of the missing assets and promised that customers would be fully reimbursed.Binance's latest update said it had now secured 95% of the stolen tokens, allowing it to begin restoring withdrawals in phases. The remaining assets are less liquid and may take longer to obtain in the required amounts.The FBI's warning about further laundering attempts comes as the exchange prepares to resume withdrawals for users affected by the incident.
Article Summary: Binance says it has secured 95% of the $6.3 billion in digital assets stolen from its platform in what is being described as the world's largest cryptocurrency heist. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has attributed the cyberattack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit. US President Donald Trump said investigators could still determine whether Pyongyang was responsible.
